citations.summary: Bounded encrypted one-hot coefficient lookup and signed 13-bit channel packing, with explicitly charged local half-gates conversion. Full ciphertext replies replace missing PackLWEs; source-only quantization, tied-head ownership and operator costs remain separate from a protected decoder.

Bounded two-party line correlations, GGM punctured keys and a full-field scalar/vector consumer. Reports distinguish dealer issuance, worker expansion, raw keys and expanded storage. Restricted-domain opening counterexamples and ring32/elementwise incompatibility remain explicit; distributed setup and decoder execution are absent.
PLLM's bounded arithmetic-garbling references adapt mixed-modulus labels and projection-gate ideas under separate one-use and plan-binding contracts.
PLLM's bounded ties-to-even rescaling and Q7 arithmetic provide related fixed-point conversion primitives; they are not an implementation of ReDASH's complete protocol.
PLLM's experimental CRT-garbled multiplication is a clean-room adaptation of the paper's arithmetic-garbling technique, not a reproduction of the complete system.
PLLM independently implements bounded one-use Boolean half-gates for private selection and arithmetic references. This is an unreviewed research backend, not a complete protected decoder.

LogRowGarbledLookup retains its fitted Q7 activation contract. LogRowGatedMultiplyQ9 separately composes a 4,096-row lookup with exact half-gates rescaling and multiplication through opaque labels. Complete client/evaluator material and boundary estimates are charged. Whole-decoder transport remains absent.

The installed CurlWaveletEncodedTable retains its bounded Q7 activation contract. CurlWaveletGatedMultiplyQ9 separately composes private Haar lookup with protected index reduction, exact up/output rescaling and a fresh product. It reports complete both-party material and four peer rounds; exact truncation replaces the paper's probabilistic protocol. Float conversion, distributed issuance and decoder transport remain open.

The installed CompactPiecewiseActivation component combines public Q7 calibration with private interval selection and Chebyshev arithmetic in a one-use half-gates circuit. Its CPU cost includes constant labels and client encodings; it is a bounded adaptation rather than the paper's MPC system.
PLLM's prepared masked-linear path and optional Freivalds verification draw on related separation and verification ideas; its protocol and trust assumptions differ from Slalom.
PLLM exposes a bounded mod-2 public-subspace leakage witness for Carnival-style masks. The control follows the later attack in Maverick, not an implementation of Carnival's protocol.
PLLM exposes KV-cache eviction as a model-neutral plan transformation. It does not yet execute the transformed plan end to end.

PLLM tests Maverick Appendix E public-subspace leakage, a bounded coded-matvec verifier and RAA numeric algebra. It has no LPN input privacy, full-width resource admission or complete Maverick delegation protocol.

The bounded CPU/Q12 masked-wire gated operator adapts SIGMA's public-gap floor shifts and residual SiLU. Its installed benchmark preserves negative quality/cost results without claiming a complete SIGMA system.
The masked-wire operator uses Grotto-style suffix-parity comparison over early-terminated Boolean DPFs, retaining independent 128-bit seeds and separate control bits.
The masked-wire operator uses Boolean-DPF lookup and sign correction with explicit correction shares; Pika's seeded distribution and complete system are not reproduced.

The installed signed-rescale helper and complete masked-wire gated block expose matched fused and unfused layouts. Multi-view fusion preserves integer outputs while reducing dependent rounds; wider comparison keys increase complete-block material. This is a scoped CPU adaptation, not FuseFSS's general compiler or GPU system.
The signed-rescale operator independently implements Figure 1 compact DCF and Section 4.1/Figure 14 interval-key sharing as selectable backends with complete material accounting.

PLLM's source-bound public equalization adapts SmoothQuant equations 3–4 with fixed alpha=3/4, normalized clipped scales and client-local activation scaling. The original fused GPU implementation and performance are not reproduced.
